title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff + regional failover + load-shedding
author: Diego Martinez
description:
Context: In high-load regional failover scenarios the SLO enforcer could thrash between backoff and failover states causing cascading load-shedding and client-facing errors. This manifested after the recent autoscaling/priority-queue change (ENG-3421) when bursts triggered rapid CB state transitions and aggressive global failovers.

This hotfix introduces a small, well-scoped set of changes to stabilize the enforcer: add a hysteresis window for backoff->normal transitions, ensure ordering guarantees when applying regional failover decisions, and tighten load-shedding thresholds for legacy clients. The change is intentionally conservative: behavior defaults are tuned to be safer and observability added so we can safely iterate.

What I changed: (summary) - Add backoff hysteresis (time-based cooldown) to slo_enforcer to prevent rapid re-entry after failover. - Ensure regional decisions are applied with a single-concurrency path to avoid race conditions between controller and legacy failover tasks. - Reduce sensitivity of legacy load-shedding path (increase queue thresholds by 20%). - Add end-to-end integration test that simulates regional overload and verifies no thrashing for 5 minutes. - Add metric tags and dashboards: slo_enforcer.backoff.hysteresis_seconds, slo_enforcer.failover.apply_count, slo_enforcer.thrash_detected. - Update runbook with rollback instructions and recommended thresholds.

Why: The incident on 2026-02-24 showed that short backoff windows + concurrent regional decisions caused oscillation and unnecessary global failovers. This increases user-visible errors and makes SLA targets unattainable during bursts. The fix reduces the transition frequency and makes decision application atomic to prevent ordering races.

Risk: Low/Medium. Behavioral change to SLO enforcer defaults (hysteresis) but covered by unit and integration tests and guarded by a feature flag. We can revert the flag if any regressions are observed.

Testing and rollout: Unit tests added for hysteresis and ordering; a 5-minute integration test that replays the incident pattern; CI passed. Rolling plan: deploy to canary, monitor slo_enforcer.thrash_detected and backoff.apply_count for 2 hours, then gradual rollout.

Related: ENG-3421, SRE-782, INT-9012.

Checklist: [x] unit tests added [x] integration test added [x] docs/runbook updated [x] metrics and dashboards defined [x] flagged behind feature flag

review_comments: Jordan Lee (reviewer): Can you justify the 30s default hysteresis? Might be too long for low-latency customers.
Author (Diego): 30s was chosen based on incident tracebacks showing oscillation ~10-20s; we picked 30s to be conservative and added a feature flag to quickly tune it.
Samira Patel (reviewer): Please add a metric to detect thrashing so we can monitor after rollout.
Author: Added slo_enforcer.thrash_detected (boolean increment) and dashboards; see observability/dashboards commit.
Evan Cho (approver): Approve after CI green and integration test stability verified in CI runs (rerun passed).
release_notes: Hotfix: Stabilize SLO enforcer by adding backoff hysteresis, serializing regional failover application to prevent race-induced thrashing, and relaxing legacy load-shedding sensitivity. Monitored via new metrics. Rollout behind feature flag.
